t.1.128.1: Then, O lord of the earth, Droṇa gathered all his pupils together, every one of them, and urged them on behalf of their teacher to provide his fee.
t.1.128.2: Seize Drupada, the king of the Pāñcālas, at the forefront of battle and bring him here; may good fortune be yours! That would be the supreme teacher's fee.
t.1.128.3: Saying "So be it," all those warriors, together with Droṇa, swiftly set out on their chariots to give their teacher his fee.
t.1.128.5: Having seized Drupada Yajñasena at the forefront of battle, together with his ministers, those bulls of the Bharatas brought him to Droṇa.
t.1.128.6: Recalling in his mind the old enmity, Droṇa spoke to Drupada, whose pride was broken, whose wealth had been seized, and who had thus come under his power.
t.1.128.4: Then those bulls among men advanced upon the Pāñcālas, slaying them as they went, and, mighty in their vigor, they crushed the city of Drupada.
t.1.128.8: Having spoken thus, he laughed at him, and having made up his mind, spoke again: "Do not be afraid for your life, O king; we brahmins are forgiving."
t.1.128.7: Having crushed your kingdom by force, I have ravaged your city as well. Now that you have fallen alive into the power of your enemy, what is wished for by way of our former friendship?
t.1.128.9: But because you played with me in the hermitage in our childhood, by that you have nurtured my affection for you, O bull among kṣatriyas.
t.1.128.10: I would seek friendship with you once again, O bull among men. I grant you a boon, O king: receive half of the kingdom.
t.1.128.11: One who is not a king, it is said, cannot be the friend of kings. Therefore, Yajñasena, I strove to win your kingdom.
t.1.128.12: You are king on the southern bank along the Bhāgīrathī, and I on the northern. Know me as your friend, O Pāñcāla, if you think it fitting.
t.1.128.14: Thus addressed, O Bhārata, Droṇa released him, and, his heart pleased, he honored him and bestowed on him half the kingdom.
t.1.128.13: This is no wonder, O brahmin, among great-souled men who are valiant. I am pleased with you, and from you I desire lasting affection.
t.1.128.15: Then he, dejected in mind, dwelt in Mākandī on the bank of the Gaṅgā, filled with country-folk, and in Kāmpilya, the finest of cities, and among the southern Pāñcālas as far as the river Carmaṇvatī.
t.1.128.16: Drupada, remembering his enmity with Droṇa, found no peace, and he saw no way to bring about Droṇa's defeat by mere kṣatriya might.
t.1.128.17: Knowing himself to be inferior in brahmanic power, and in might as well, the king, seeking the birth of a son, nursed that grievance; and Droṇa took possession of the land of Ahicchattra.
t.1.128.18: Thus, O king, the city of Ahicchatrā, together with its countryside, was conquered in battle by Pārtha and handed over to Droṇa.
